thread:
Sara Li: Heads-up — ACME prod (dedicated d-42) opened a ticket: sudden throughput drop ~40% and increased 429s since ~02:00 UTC. Customer sees p95 latency go from 120ms -> 480ms. Attaching their example request IDs.

Oncall-bot: Alert: dedicated-capacity-d-42.high-429-rate at 2026-03-17T02:04:12Z — link: https://internal.alerts/redwood/alerts/8921 :rotating_light:

Mike Johnson: Looking at recent deploys — no code push to runtime at that window. Any autoscale events?

Cheng Wu: Checking metrics quickly. continuous_queue_depth jumped around 02:01 UTC and stayed high. Snapshot from our metrics API: 
```
continuous_queue_depth{pool="d-42"}  74 -> 962
avg_batch_size{pool="d-42"}       18 -> 4
max_batch_tokens                 512
p99_token_latency(ms)            120 -> 870
```
Seems like batches are getting starved and we spin more small batches, throughput drops.

Alex Patel: Could be payload size distribution changed — customer mentioned switching to long-context prompts yesterday. If individual requests have higher token lengths, they hit max_batch_tokens and reduce batching efficiency.

Priya Nair: I grabbed a sample trace for request id req-ACME-3345: KV cache hit rate unchanged, but scheduler shows a high enqueue->dispatch gap. Scheduler logs: 
```
[02:03:45] enqueue request=req-ACME-3345 tokens=620
[02:03:45] queued
[02:03:46] dispatched batch_size=2 total_tokens=1240
```
We often want batch_size >= 8 for good throughput on this model.

Sara Li: Customer also reported intermittent 401s earlier this morning — could be retry storms? But ticket shows 429s mainly. Can ops confirm no auth service blips?

Mike Johnson: Auth service OK — no spike in 401s correlating to d-42 window. Billing subsystem had a brief error at 01:58 UTC unrelated (invoice job), not linked.

Cheng Wu: Hypothesis: continuous-batcher window mis-calculated due to increased token counts and our scheduler’s max_batch_tokens fixed at 512. When requests exceed that, they force small batches or immediate dispatch causing inefficient packing. Also saw scheduler preemption of larger batches because of deadline skew.

Alex Patel: Quick repro plan: run synthetic workload with mixed token sizes reflecting ACME traffic: 30% >600 tokens, 70% <150 tokens. Observe average batch_size and throughput. I can run in staging on pool s-04 with same kernel config.

Priya Nair: Temporary mitigation we can push to customer: set their per-req max_context to 512 or enable request-side truncation. But we should also consider scheduler tuning: increase max_batch_tokens to 1024 temporarily and allow longer batch wait (batch_window_ms +30ms) for this pool.

Mike Johnson: I'll open a short-lived config flag to increase max_batch_tokens for d-42 and extend batch_window_ms by 25ms. Rolling this to a single AZ first. If that improves avg_batch_size and p95, we can keep it.

Cheng Wu: Also adding metrics dashboards to surface token-length distribution per-customer. Right now it's global and hard to correlate.

Sara Li: Customer accepted temporary truncation for now. Mike, Cheng — coordinate the config change and post graphs. I'll update the ticket.

Oncall-bot: Deployment scheduled by Mike Johnson at 2026-03-17T02:20:00Z — rolling to az-1.

Mike Johnson: Pushing change now. Patch diff: 
```
- max_batch_tokens: 512
- batch_window_ms: 25
+ max_batch_tokens: 1024
+ batch_window_ms: 50
```
Applying to pool d-42 (az-1) only.

Cheng Wu: After patch: continuous_queue_depth dropped from ~900 -> ~120 within 90s. avg_batch_size rose 4 -> 10. p95 down to ~150ms. Initial customer confirmation: "latency looks back to normal" :thumbsup:

Priya Nair: Leaving monitoring on for 1h, will rollback if any regression (e.g., token-latency p99).

Sara Li: Good job. Follow-ups: (1) add per-customer token distribution metric, (2) scheduler should consider token_count-aware batching and soft deadlines, (3) update runbook with steps for similar incidents. Closing when stable for 2h.

Mike Johnson: Noted. I'll paste post-deploy graphs and the staging repro steps in the ticket.

Alex Patel: Repro artifacts: synthetic runner command: 
```
python tools/synth_load.py --pool s-04 --mix "0.3:700,0.7:120" --rps 60 --duration 600s
```
Used to validate change locally.

Sara Li: Thanks team. I'll keep the ticket open until 04:30 UTC and then mark resolved if stable.
